taxonomic_note: Current Kew POWO accepts Cercis canadensis subsp. texensis. The older Texas usage C. canadensis var. texensis is a synonym.
look_here_first: Look for the thick glossy leathery leaves. Texas redbud has broad rounded to kidney-shaped leaves with a noticeably shiny upper surface, generally less wavy-edged and larger than Mexican redbud.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Master Plant Pool Hays-local source for the Texas redbud row. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Fabaceae index includes C. canadensis var. texensis. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a dedicated county treatment of C. canadensis var. texensis.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Historical variety records are accepted for the current subspecies because Kew explicitly treats var. texensis as a synonym.

best_field_traits: small deciduous tree or large shrub
broad rounded to reniform leaf shape
leaf margins generally less wavy than Mexican redbud
rose-pink flowers appearing on older wood before leaves
dry limestone woodland and canyon habitat
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with subsp. mexicana, subsp. texensis usually has larger, less wavy, glossier leaves and occupies Central Texas east of the more xeric Mexican-redbud range.

photo_strategy.target_count: 2 core diagnostic views now; add pod/bark macro later only if useful
photo_strategy.visual_priority: glossy broad less-wavy foliage + spring flowers / new leaves
photo_strategy.comparison_note: Teach against Mexican redbud using leaf size, gloss, and margin waviness.
